title: Leukemia can be Effectively Early Predicted in Routine Physical Examination with the Assistance of Machine Learning Models
summary: Random forest and XGBoost applied to routine examination/lab data distinguished newly diagnosed leukemia cases from healthy controls and identified influential blood measures.
ai_technology: Random forest and XGBoost classify leukemia cases from routine examination and laboratory measurements.
organization: Department of Hematology, The First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing 400016, China.

evidence.tested: The study reports accuracy above 0.9 and highlights RBC, hematocrit, and WBC measures in a specific early-detection task.
evidence.unknown: Internal train/test data from one hospital with selected cases and healthy controls; no independent external cohort, so performance may not transfer to screening populations.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest and XGBoost classify leukemia cases from routine examination and laboratory measurements.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
